key_insight: CAAMP is a large longitudinal Amish cohort that combines cognition, family history, genetics, and biomarkers to uncover factors linked to aging, dementia, and successful aging.
clinical_relevance: The study can help identify genetic and biological signals that may improve understanding of Alzheimer disease risk, protection, and age-related cognitive decline in older adults.
method: Enrolled 3,978 Amish participants across Ohio and Indiana sites
Performed clinical, cognitive, functional, and informant-based consensus adjudication of cognitive status
Collected pedigree, genomic, biospecimen, biomarker, and longitudinal assessment data
evidence_signal: The cohort has 2,928 participants with adjudicated cognitive status, with 66.6% cognitively unimpaired and 8.9% diagnosed with Alzheimer disease at the latest assessment.
watch_item: Findings from a founder population may not generalize to more diverse populations, and many participants still lacked detailed cognitive evaluation at enrollment.
paper_title: A longitudinal study of age-related traits and cognitive function: The Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project (CAAMP)
